newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index closes up on economic optimism.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index closes up on economic optimism.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares ended higher on Wednesday on optimism about China's economic outlook and strong performances of several individual stocks, brokers said.
The B share index gained 1.04 points or 0.64 percent to end at 163.12 points on thin turnover of HK$85 million, compared with Tuesday's HK$172.8 million.
"The central bank governor's strong economic forecast coupled with the absense of bad news lifted the market mood," a trader at Central-South Securities said.
"No news is good news," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said, referring to last week's talk of a securities clampdown that depressed the B index.

China's inflation rate is expected to be low in 1997, enabling the central bank to focus on reforming monetary controls and reducing unhealthy assets, central bank governor Dai Xianglong was quoted by the official media as saying.
Dai forecast China's inflation rate at lower than the six percent target in 1997, compared with 1996's 6.5 percent, the newspaper said.
Good performance of several stocks also cheered the market, analysts said.
"Tellus, Wafangdian and Jiangling all boosted morale today," an analyst at Sun Hung Kai Investment Services Ltd in Shenzhen said.
Shenzhen Tellus Machinery & Electronics Co Ltd surged to its 10 percent limit-up on Wednesday, rising HK$0.33 to HK$3.64 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Analysts said talk that the company would soon announce good 1996 annual results pulled the share up.
"Investors are buying on talk that the company has turned from a loss to a profit in 1996," the Sun Hung Kai analyst said, adding he expected the company results to be published soon.
Traders said Wafangdian Bearing Co Ltd, which closed up 88.72 percent on its first day of trade on Tuesday, also helped boost investor.
"Wafangdian's performance excited the market," a trader at J&A Securities said.
Wafangdian ended Wednesday at HK$5.16, up HK$0.14 or 2.79 percent on volume of 5.6 million shares. Its issue price was HK$2.66.
Jiangling Motors Corp said it planned to issue 170 million new B shares of which 120 million shares would be sold to Ford Motor Co.
Investors welcome the move as a stamp of foreign confidence in China's motor industry, analyst said.
However, concerns about company results in the reporting season limited gains, analysts said.
"Some investors are excited about the results, some are wary, but I think most are holding back from heavy investments," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Only three out of the 44 B share companies listed in Shenzhen have made their 1996 results public, with the official April 30 deadline ahead.
The rise in U.S. interest rates is also seen capping B share gains, traders said.
The A share index ended the day up at 451.81 points, rising 6.65 points or 1.49 percent on turnover of 13.3 billion yuan against Tuesday's 13.8 billion yuan.
